w:r.w:t: This deployment introduces the IDB_BEHAVIORAL_SCN package update for the Islamic Development Bank, specifically targeting the BEH_HAIRCUT_DELAYED_PAYMNT_SCN procedure. This procedure handles
ALM custom scenarios that combine delayed payment modelling with haircut adjustments across the ALM system.

The procedure operates in three logical layers. First, it restores interest cashflows in the CFL table by copying base scenario values (LIQ_BASE_SCENARIO) into haircut-delayed scenarios and zeroing out any additional interest rows that do not exist in the base. Second, it aligns the T_ALM_BUCKETS table by overwriting interest and non-interest fields from the base scenario while preserving haircut principal amounts, then recalculates total inflows, outflows, gaps, and cumulative gaps. Third, it propagates these final values into the TIME_SEGMENT_RESULT table to ensure consistent reporting across all haircut-delayed scenario views.
The package contains a separate procedure (BEH_DELAYED_PAYMNT_SCN) for standard delayed payment scenarios. This deployment document covers only the haircut-specific procedure.

Before executing the deployment, confirm the following:
Ensure access to the Central Schema in the target database environment.
Confirm that SQL Developer (or equivalent) is available and connected.
Verify that the existing IDB_BEHAVIORAL_SCN package header and body scripts are accessible for backup.
Confirm that tables CFL, T_ALM_BUCKETS, and TIME_SEGMENT_RESULT are accessible in the schema.
Confirm that SCN_DEF and CONTEXTS lookup tables are populated for the reporting date and workspace.
After deployment, verify the following to confirm successful installation:
Confirm the IDB_BEHAVIORAL_SCN package compiles without errors in the target schema.
Validate that procedure BEH_HAIRCUT_DELAYED_PAYMNT_SCN is visible under the package.
Execute a test run against a non-production reporting date and inspect CFL, T_ALM_BUCKETS, and TIME_SEGMENT_RESULT for expected values.
Confirm no compilation errors appear in the DBA_ERRORS view for the IDB_BEHAVIORAL_SCN object.
Perform the following steps in sequence on the target database environment (Central Schema):
Open SQL Developer and connect to the Central Schema using the appropriate credentials.
Take a backup of the existing IDB_BEHAVIORAL_SCN package header (PKS) by exporting the current DDL from the schema.
Take a backup of the existing IDB_BEHAVIORAL_SCN package body (PKB) by exporting the current DDL from the schema.
Open the updated IDB_BEHAVIORAL_SCN.PKS (package header) script in SQL Developer and execute it against the Central Schema.
Open the updated IDB_BEHAVIORAL_SCN.PKB (package body) script in SQL Developer and execute it against the Central Schema.
Verify that the package compiles without errors by checking the compilation status in SQL Developer or querying DBA_ERRORS.
Confirm that both BEH_DELAYED_PAYMNT_SCN and BEH_HAIRCUT_DELAYED_PAYMNT_SCN procedures are accessible within the deployed package.

There is NO requirement for any downtime. This deployment involves only DDL changes to an Oracle PL/SQL package and does not require the ALM application or any related services to be stopped. The package can be compiled and deployed during normal working hours without impact
technical team. Deployment can be performed during normal working hours given that no system downtime is required. It is recommended to coordinate the execution timing with the
ALM operations team to avoid conflicts with scheduled ALM processing runs.

This deployment updates CFL interest cashflows, ALM bucket results, and time segment results for all scenarios that match the pattern DELAYED + HAIRCUT. The procedure copies base scenario interest values into haircut-delayed scenarios, zeros out extra interest cashflow rows
recalculates aggregated totals across all affected reporting dimensions.
The following tables are directly updated by this deployment:
Cash Flow Ledger — Interest cashflows are restored from base scenario and extra haircut interest rows are zeroed out
ALM time bucket results — Interest/non-interest fields are overwritten from base scenario; principal remains from haircut scenario; totals and cumulative gap are recalculated
Time segment summary results — Aligned from final T_ALM_BUCKETS values for all haircut delayed scenarios
No structural or schema-level changes (DDL) are made to any of the tables listed above. All changes are data-level updates (DML) performed via MERGE and UPDATE statements within the procedure.
Before deployment, backups of the existing IDB_BEHAVIORAL_SCN package header and body must be taken as described in the Installation Steps section.

a rollback is required, the previous package header and body scripts can be re-executed in SQL Developer to restore the prior state of the package. No rollback scripts for data changes are required, as the procedure's DML operations are idempotent — re-running the prior package version against the same data will restore the expected state.
